newsitem.title: GERMANY: Holzmann supervisory board head resigns.
newsitem.headline: Holzmann supervisory board head resigns.

text.p: Philipp Holzmann AG, Germany's largest construction group, said on Tuesday the head of its supervisory board, Hermann Becker, had resigned.

Holzmann said that a successor to Becker, 70, would be chosen at an extraordinary meeting of the supervisory board on April 10. German supervisory boards have a similar advisory role to that of the board of directors at U.S. companies.
Supervisory board member Carl von Boehm-Bezing, also a member of the main board of Deutsche Bank had indicated he is ready to take up the position, Holzmann said.
Holzmann and Hochtief, Germany's second largest builder, are currently involved in plans to cooperate more closely, particularly on international projects.

Hochtief's efforts in the past to increase its existing 20 percent stake in Holzmann to 35 percent have been vetoed by German cartel authorities, which fear too great a concentration of the German construction market in one company.
